definition: OMIM #620511 designates Fliedner-Zweier syndrome (FZS), an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the SCAF4 gene. The clinical presentation is highly variable and characterized predominantly by developmental delay with speech impairment, cognitive abilities ranging from normal intelligence to severe intellectual disability (most often borderline to mild), seizures, and skeletal abnormalities such as scoliosis, clubfoot, or hip dysplasia.
